gaps.sentence: He's not used to ___ so early.
gaps.explanation: be used TO + -ing: not used to getting (it's a habit he isn't accustomed to).

gaps.sentence: I look forward to ___ you at the reunion.
gaps.explanation: 'To' is a preposition here, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: She suggested ___ the meeting until Monday.
She can't afford ___ her car repaired this month.
gaps.explanation: afford + to-infinitive: can't afford to get.

gaps.sentence: The teacher made us ___ the whole essay again.
gaps.explanation: 'Make someone do' — active 'make' takes the bare infinitive.

gaps.sentence: We spent the whole morning ___ for tickets.
gaps.explanation: spend time + -ing: spent the morning queueing.

gaps.sentence: When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)
